draft.title: The setting of Pompeii and Herculaneum
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum were Roman towns on the Bay of Naples, in Campania, on the west coast of Italy. Both lay close to Mount Vesuvius, a volcano.
a larger, busy trading town. It stood near the mouth of the river Sarno, which helped goods move to and from the sea.
a smaller seaside town. It was a quieter place, with many fine houses facing the bay.
The soil near Vesuvius was fertile, so farms around the towns grew crops such as grapes and olives. The people had no clear sign that Vesuvius was a danger.
draft.remember: Two towns on one bay under Vesuvius: Pompeii for trade, Herculaneum by the sea.

a.q: Which description of the two towns is correct?
opts: Pompeii was a busy trading town, Herculaneum a small seaside one
Herculaneum was a busy trading town, Pompeii a small seaside one
Both were small farming villages far from the coast
Both were inland military camps on the slopes of Vesuvius
a.why: Pompeii was the larger town and a centre of trade, while Herculaneum was smaller and lay by the sea. The reversed option is tempting, but it swaps the two towns.
a.clue: Think about which town was larger and which was smaller.

b.q: Lucia is a trader in Campania. She wants to ship wine and oil to buyers in many places. Why would the town of Pompeii suit her?
opts: It was a busy trading town with a link to the sea
It was a small, quiet town with few visitors
It was a seaside town known mostly for its fine houses
It was a town sited high up on the slopes of Vesuvius
b.why: Pompeii was a busy trading town, and the river Sarno helped goods reach the sea. Herculaneum was the seaside town with fine houses, but it was smaller and quieter, so it suits her aim less well.
b.clue: Which town was the busy one for trade?

problems.detail: "The people had no clear sign that Vesuvius was a danger" overstates the case. The major earthquake of AD 62/63 and later tremors were warning signs, even though people did not link them to the volcano. Year 12 students are expected to know this. Better: "People did not recognise the signs that Vesuvius was a danger."
